She kept looking at him, trying to catch his eye, and he kept dodging, like he thought if he really looked, something bad might happen. You ever see someone do that? Like, they’re right there, but they’re trying so hard not to actually be? Raskolnikov was like that. He’d mumble a few words, then clam up, his chin practically buried in his chest, and honestly, it made the air thick.

The thing is, Zossimov started talking, but it was one of those monologues where you’re not sure if he expects anyone to reply. He said, “Well, I suppose the weather’s cleared up, though I can’t say I noticed.” And then he laughed, but it was just a noise, no real joy in it. Dounia half-smiled, as if to encourage him, but her eyes drifted back to Raskolnikov, asking questions with her gaze that most folks wouldn’t ever ask out loud. What was he thinking? Why wouldn’t he just speak openly? Does anybody really ever know what’s going on in another person’s head?

Suddenly, Raskolnikov muttered something about needing air, which was funny, because the windows were wide open already. Zossimov, who had been staring at a crack in the glass, just shrugged. “Sure, go ahead,” he said, as though he was granting permission, but then he looked at Dounia and his eyebrows kind of lifted, like he wanted her to say something to anchor Raskolnikov in place. She didn’t, though. Either she didn’t know what to say, or she chose not to. Sometimes silence is, I don’t know, sharper than words.

The room felt bigger when Raskolnikov left, but also emptier, as if his presence had filled up more space than really seemed possible. Dounia pressed her hands together, her knuckles turning white. And honestly, you could feel her worry, hanging in the air like a question mark. Zossimov moved over to the table, picking up a book and flipping through it, only he wasn’t reading, just pretending to. It’s weird, right, how people do stuff to avoid actually dealing with things? Like, sometimes you’d rather look busy than admit you’ve got no clue what to do.

So, I guess, you know, I haven't really told you much about that trip down the Rhine, have I? The thing is, everyone talks about how beautiful it is, but until you've actually stood with your feet just hanging over the edge of a rickety old wooden dock with fog curling off the water, well, you just don't know. You just don't get it. I mean, some mornings the sun tries to break through, and you get these, uh, rays, just slicing the mist, lighting up the water and making everything else look kinda gloomy by comparison. That's the Rhine for you. One minute it's all bright and sparkling, almost showing off, and the next it's pulling somber, with gray cliffs and little villages that look like they're hiding secrets.

So, Clerval—my friend, yeah, the one who's always in a hurry to see everything—he kept dragging me from town to town. We'd barely get a look at, I dunno, maybe a crumbling old tower, and he'd already want to run ahead to the next ruin. I tried to tell him, like, "Hey, slow down, we've got, you know, days." But he always grinned at me, like I was missing something important if I didn't see every church and listen to every story spinning out of a local's mouth. There's just, I guess, a kind of restlessness in people sometimes. Have you ever felt that way? Like you just can't get enough, no matter how many beautiful moments you stack up, you want one more, and then one after that?

I remember this time when we reached Strasburgh, and the streets were all stone and shadow, with balconies spilling over with geraniums—red ones, the kind that almost look fake because they're so bright. I don't know why, but I felt like I'd seen that city before, even though I'd never set foot there. Maybe it was just the stories Clerval had been telling all morning, or maybe it was the way the river curled right past the black-and-white timbered houses. He said it was like stepping into a painting, and honestly, he wasn't wrong.

But here's the thing—sometimes, I wished the towns would just stop coming, at least for a little while. There was this hour, late in the day, when the sun would dip behind those big, rolling hills, and everything just went hush. You could hear the water slap gently against the boat, or maybe if you listened hard enough, you'd catch a far-off bell. I thought about writing down what I saw, you know, keeping a record so I wouldn't forget, but, I dunno, it felt like putting a butterfly under glass. You lose something that way, don't you? Is it better to try to hold onto every detail, or just let it pass through you and trust that the really important parts will stick?

We met all sorts of people as we floated down the river—an old woman in Koblenz with hands like knots, who insisted we try her apple cake, which tasted like cinnamon and river air somehow, and a skinny kid with a battered violin who played just for us on a bridge, the notes floating up and getting tangled in the poplars. Clerval liked to talk to everyone, and I liked to listen, mostly. It's funny how you can feel at home with strangers, especially when they're smiling at you over slices of cake or nodding as you pass by, like they know you're just another wanderer who can't quite explain why they're there to anyone, not even themselves.

Some nights, lying in whatever noisy little inn we'd found, I'd stare at the ceiling and try to piece together all the things we'd seen that day—gloomy castles half-swallowed by ivy, wide-open fields with cows as still as clouds, and fishermen casting lines while church bells rang out something that could have been a warning or just the sign of evening. It all blurred together sometimes, and I'd wonder, what does it matter if I saw every beautiful thing, if I couldn't keep it all inside me? Maybe it's enough that we were there, that we watched the Rhine move on and took a little bit of its music with us. Or maybe, I don't know, maybe it's just the kind of trip that stays in your bones, even after you've forgotten the stories.

On Monday, Alexei Navalny was found in a remote colony in the Arctic Circle, Russian officials said. For several weeks before, his relatives and lawyers could not communicate with him. His supporters in Moscow had concerns about his health and safety. The officials insisted Navalny was being held according to Russian law. Still, many international observers criticized the conditions and the secrecy around his transfer.

Navalny, a well-known Russian opposition leader, was moved from a penal colony near Vladimir to this facility in Yamalo-Nenets region. Russian authorities confirmed the transfer took place mid-December. His lawyer said he learned of the new location only after repeated requests for information. CNN reported that Navalny’s supporters called the new prison “one of the most severe in Russia.”

Navalny’s team said communication with him is now almost impossible. His lawyer described how the colony is difficult to reach. The nearest town is hundreds of kilometers away. Weather conditions make travel unpredictable. Human rights activists said this makes it harder to monitor Navalny’s treatment or help him if needed.

The new colony is called IK-3. It is sometimes referred to as “Polar Wolf.” Former prisoners and human rights defenders said the facility is known for strict rules and harsh discipline. CNN obtained statements from people who had served their sentences there. They described limited access to outside information and very poor conditions. Navalny’s allies said they are afraid he will face increased pressure.

Navalny’s mother said in an interview with a Russian news outlet that she worries about her son’s health. She told reporters that he already had health problems before the transfer. She said now he will face severe cold and isolation. The authorities said Navalny receives medical attention as needed. They denied all allegations of mistreatment.

Mikhail Khodorkovsky, a former Russian oligarch who also spent years in Russian detention, made a statement about Navalny. He said on social media that prisoners are often sent to very remote areas as punishment. Khodorkovsky said it is difficult for lawyers and family to visit such prisons, which he called a way for authorities to cut off prisoners from the outside world. He called for more international pressure on Russian officials regarding Navalny’s situation.

Navalny’s lawyers tried to visit him several times in December but were turned away. They said officials gave contradictory explanations for why they could not enter the colony. Sometimes they were told Navalny was “not available,” other times they were told the prison was on lockdown due to quarantine. The lawyers said they are considering a formal complaint.

The Russian penal service responded to questions from journalists. They said Navalny is being held in conditions similar to other prisoners. They stated that any claims about violations of his rights are not true. However, activists said the secrecy and lack of access point to possible problems. One activist told CNN that when a prisoner is isolated so completely, there is a risk for abuse.

Navalny is serving a long sentence for what he calls politically motivated charges. He was arrested in 2021 after returning to Russia from Germany. In Germany, he was recovering from poisoning, which he and many Western governments blamed on the Kremlin. The Russian government denied these accusations.

The United States, the European Union, and other countries have called for Navalny’s release. They said his continued detention is a sign of growing repression in Russia. Russian officials replied these statements are foreign interference. They said Navalny’s case is only about following the law.

Navalny’s supporters in Moscow organized small protests. Police quickly broke up the gatherings. Many of Navalny’s top aides have already left Russia, fearing arrest. The political climate for opposition is tense. Ordinary people said they are afraid to talk openly about Navalny.

Khodorkovsky and other former prisoners said the authorities use the penal system to silence political opponents. The transfer to remote colonies is an old method. Even so, Navalny’s team said they will continue their efforts to keep his case in public view.

Navalny’s lawyer said he hopes to visit the colony again soon. He told reporters that for now, only official information is available. The isolation of the colony makes independent confirmation impossible. International organizations called for immediate access to Navalny.

For now, concern about Navalny’s fate continues. His supporters said they would not stop speaking about his imprisonment. Russian officials have made no sign they plan to move him from the Arctic colony. The world watches for more news from the remote north.

The number of rats seems to be increasing in London, according to several pest control experts. They say more reports have come in about rats being noticed during the day as well as night. Residents and business owners are speaking more often about rats showing up near homes, shops, and restaurants. Some people have sent pictures to local councils. In these photos, rats can be seen near bins, in parks, and sometimes inside buildings. Experts believe that construction projects in London have disturbed rat nests underground. When nests are disturbed, rats look for new places. They move to areas with food and shelter.

Food waste is a main reason for the rat problem. According to technicians who deal with pests, rats are attracted to bags and containers outside buildings. Restaurants and cafes sometimes leave bags out overnight. Rats tear these bags open and eat what they find inside. Experts say that smaller businesses do not always use proper bins. Some bins are broken or missing lids. When bins are not closed well, rats can get in easily. Many people in the pest control industry think that the city needs to clean more often. If trash is left out, rats will come.

The rainy weather in London also causes trouble. When there is heavy rain, rats come out from their hiding places because their nests become too wet. Pest specialists say that after rain, their phones ring more often. People complain about rats running near houses, schools, and shops. Rat numbers can become worse during wet periods. A worker from a pest control company said, “When it rains, rats are forced to move. They look for dry places. They are not picky. They will go anywhere, even homes.” Several companies agreed that calls increase after storms.

Some neighborhoods suffer more than others. Areas with older buildings are at higher risk. Old buildings have cracks and holes in the walls. Rats can squeeze through small gaps. Once inside, they search for scraps or crumbs. Houses with pets sometimes leave pet food out. Rats will eat dog food or cat food if they find it. Families tell local news they worry about disease. Rats carry germs that can cause sickness. One woman from East London said, “We see them in our backyard. My children are scared. We do not want rats in our house.” Another man said, “I have seen them outside the shop almost every day. It is bad for business.”

London councils have tried to solve the rat issue for some time. Many councils hire pest control services. These services place traps and poison around problem spots. Some people say poison is dangerous for pets and birds. Animal activists do not like the use of poison. They suggest safer methods, but these are slower and cost more. Council members explain that the rat problem may not be solved soon. As long as there is food left outside, rats will come back. Local officials advise citizens to put rubbish in bins and not leave food out. They ask business owners to keep bins closed.

There are also stories about rats getting inside the Tube. Passengers sometimes see rats running across platforms or tracks. Transport staff try to keep stations clean. Still, rats find ways inside. Engineers say that rats can live in tunnels and passageways. The underground is warm and offers many hidden spots. Sometimes, rats chew electrical wires. This causes disruptions. Transport for London admitted that rats are sometimes seen in stations. They said, “We clean every day. We do what we can, but rats are smart. They find new places to hide.” Commuters are told to report any sightings.

Pest control technicians are busy. One company said that calls about rats have doubled in the last year. They now send workers to homes, offices, and shops almost every day. They check where rats are coming in. They put traps and block holes. Some workers use cameras to find nests. Sometimes they discover several nests in one street. Workers wear masks and gloves for safety. They explain that rats are not always afraid of people. Rats become braver when they are hungry. A technician said, “Rats used to hide. Now they are seen during the day. They just walk by people.”

The government has given some money to councils to help control rats. This money pays for more traps and extra cleaning. Some councils have set up education programs. They teach people not to leave food and to tidy waste. Schools are told not to leave packed lunches outside. Shop owners are given leaflets with instructions. The city also considers making new rules. These rules may tell businesses to use stronger bins and clean more often. Some local politicians say that more effort is needed. They believe that only a city-wide plan will help.

Andújar kept steady and won the second set 7-5.

Fans were surprised. Thiem was a favorite for the open. He had won important titles in the past years. His return to the court was awaited by supporters. After a long injury, everyone was hoping to see his best level. But on this Sunday, his game was not enough. His backhand shots missed often. He also made mistakes near the net.

Andújar said it was a hard match. He respected Thiem and knew the game would be close. He stayed confident after losing a few games in the second set. He said he trusted his serve and tried to keep putting pressure on Thiem. Andújar also said the stadium noise gave him extra energy.

Thiem told journalists he was disappointed. He said his form was not perfect yet. He promised to practice more and come back stronger. He thanked the audience for support, even when he was behind. Thiem said he would learn from the loss and not give up.

For Thiem, the tournament is over, but many think he can return to his best soon. The open continues with more surprise results possible. The fans look forward to seeing who will become champion.

On Monday, many people gathered at the community hall in central Honolulu. There was excitement and also worry. The Hawaii State Language Committee met to talk about HSL. Hawaii Sign Language, or HSL, has a long but quiet history. Few people know about this language. Many think that American Sign Language is the only way for deaf people to communicate. But in Hawaii, this is not the full truth.

Kaleo Lambrecht, who is 52, spoke to the group. He used HSL with strong movements. His mother, Lani Lambrecht, explained with her voice. “My son always used HSL at home. He learned it from my father, who was born in 1920. We did not know about American Sign Language. Only HSL,” she said.

Many deaf people in Hawaii share this story. Their families learned HSL many years ago, before ASL was brought to the schools. HSL is different from ASL. Some words look the same, but much is not the same. People say it is its own language.

Scholars from the University of Hawaii started to study HSL in 2011. Dr. James Green, a linguist, shared findings at the meeting. He said, “We have found that HSL is unique. It has its own grammar and signs. It is not the same as ASL. HSL came from the deaf community in Hawaii. It is a local creation. But now, fewer than 30 people use it fluently.”

Many who use HSL are old. Young people do not learn it. At the Hawaii School for the Deaf and Blind in Honolulu, teachers use American Sign Language. This is the national norm. Students there may hear about HSL, but they learn standard ASL.

Eileen Kamaka, who grew up deaf on Kauai, remembers her first time at this school. “I was 8 years old when I came to Honolulu. My home signs were HSL. But at school, all the teachers signed ASL. Other children already knew ASL. I felt lost."

Others had the same feeling. Some teachers told students that HSL was wrong. They said it was an old way and not correct. “This made many children ashamed of HSL,” says Lani Lambrecht. “They stopped using it. They did not teach it to their children.”

Now, people are trying to save HSL. The committee asks the state to help. They want classes in HSL, books, and videos. Some ask for HSL to be taught alongside ASL at the deaf school. There is hope that young deaf children could learn both.

The state has promised to look at the issue. Thomas Okana, who works for the Department of Education, said, “We know about the problem. We want to respect Hawaii’s history. But we must think how to add HSL. We have few teachers for HSL. Also, we must talk with families. Many parents only know ASL.”

Parents are worried about confusion. Some ask if students will become mixed up with two sign languages. Dr. Green says this will not be a big problem. “Children in many countries learn more than one language,” he says. “They are smart. They understand when to use which language. HSL is important for Hawaiian culture.”

The committee also wants recognition of HSL as an official state language. Some say this will help the language to survive. It would make Hawaii the first state in the US with two official sign languages.

But not all agree. Some school leaders say resources are too few. They say schools already struggle. “We need more teachers. We need updated materials. Adding a second sign language is not easy,” says Rachel Lee, principal of the deaf school.

Parents of young deaf children want strong support for ASL. They say it helps children to join in the wider world. “My son can use ASL to speak with deaf people everywhere in America,” says Ana Souza, whose child is six. “HSL is interesting, but he needs ASL to have more choices.”

But for the Lambrecht family, this is about more than school. “HSL is like Hawaiian language. It is ours,” says Lani. Her son, Kaleo, adds with his hands, “My grandfather’s hands told stories. If nobody learns HSL, those stories become lost.”

The committee is working with the university. They record the stories of older HSL users. They take videos and make sign dictionaries. They hope this will help future children learn.

Some efforts happen at home. Aunty Malia, who is 80 and deaf, teaches her grandchildren signs. “I use HSL with them when they visit me. They laugh and copy me. I think they remember,” she says with a smile.

The national conference of Catholic bishops ended yesterday with a statement concerning the handling of sexual abuse within the Church. The bishops met for three days in the capital. During several sessions, the topic of abuse was raised many times. The bishops read letters from victims and listened to their stories. It was announced early in the conference that the Church must do more to protect children and vulnerable adults.

In their final statement, the bishops admitted mistakes were made in the past. They said some priests had committed sexual abuse. The statement also said some bishops did not act when they learned of the abuse. The bishops apologized for this and asked forgiveness. They promised to listen better to victims in the future.

According to the statement, the Church will now have stricter procedures. Every case of alleged sexual abuse will be reported to both Church authorities and civil authorities. Bishops will have less power to decide these matters alone. A national commission will be set up to review all old and new cases.

The conference was attended by over two hundred bishops from all regions. Some bishops spoke publicly during the meeting, others gave interviews to the media. Bishop Marcos Duarte, who is from the north, said, "This crisis hurt many people. We cannot allow this to happen again." Other bishops, such as Bishop Maria del Sol, said the new procedures are only a first step. She said, "We must create a new culture in the Church, where the voice of victims is heard without fear."

Survivor groups also sent messages to the conference. They asked for more action and less words. Some survivors met directly with bishops. They said the bishops must publish names of all priests who were accused, not only the names of those found guilty in court. The bishops did not agree to publish all names, but said they will study the question.

During the conference, several prayers were said for the victims of abuse. The bishops wore purple sashes, a color of mourning, as a symbol of sorrow and repentance. At the main session hall, a candle burned all day. It was to remember those harmed in the Church.

The bishops' statement did not please all observers. Some Catholic lay groups said it is too late for apologies. They demanded more resignations from bishops who hid abuse cases in their dioceses. In some regions, members of the Church protested outside the conference. They called for more transparency and less secrecy.

In a press conference after the meeting, the conference president, Bishop Juan Franco, spoke for the group. He said, "It is not easy for us to face our failures. But we must. We know the pain of the victims is deep. We can only move forward if we change our ways." Bishop Franco repeated that the national commission will have independent members, not only bishops and priests. He also said the Church will cooperate with police investigations.

Many priests who attended the conference said they support the changes. Some young priests said they feel shame for the actions of others in the past. Others said they hope the Church can now begin to heal. Outside the conference, some ordinary Catholics told journalists they have lost trust in their leaders. They want to see real action, not just words.

The bishops announced there will be a follow-up meeting in six months. At that time, they will report on progress with the new procedures. They also promised to meet again with survivor groups. The bishops said they will pray together for all in the Church who suffer.

International observers also commented on the conference. Some said it was a step in the right direction, but not enough. Others warned that without real change, the Church could lose many members. In some neighboring countries, Catholic bishops are also facing similar crises.

At the end of the conference, the bishops left the building in silence. They did not wave to cameras. Many looked down. Some wiped away tears. The purple candle was still burning. The statement was read again on national radio. Many people listened. The question remains if this moment will bring real change or if it will be another promise soon forgotten. The victims and the faithful are waiting. For now, the Church’s leaders have spoken, and the nation watches for the next step.

Local authorities reported at least twelve people missing, while search and rescue teams worked throughout the day. The collapse happened around 6:30 am, when most residents were still inside. Emergency crews pulled several survivors from the rubble, but feared others could still be trapped. The city’s mayor visited the site and told reporters the cause of the collapse was not clear. He said structural engineers would inspect the debris and check if mistakes occurred during construction.

The building was six stories high, made of poured concrete. Residents said they had noticed small cracks in walls and ceilings in recent months. Some said they reported their concerns to the building management, but no repairs were done. One resident, Mrs. Gupta, told a local TV channel she complained about water leaks and uneven floors, but got no answer. The building was about 25 years old. Officials said it passed routine inspections last year. However, a retired engineer who visited the scene said the concrete looked weak and the steel bars inside were rusted. He explained that poor maintenance and water seeping into the structure could have led to the disaster.

By evening, three bodies were recovered, and five people were pulled out alive. Hospital officials said two were in critical condition.

He said, "We see cracks, too, but nobody listens when we complain."

Experts explained how building collapses can happen. They said not enough steel inside concrete columns makes them weak. Water can also damage the concrete, making it soft. Sometimes, too much weight on upper floors can be dangerous. In this city, several old buildings have had problems in the past. Some were repaired, others were simply painted over to look better. After Tuesday's collapse, officials promised stricter checks. The mayor told the press, "We will do our best to prevent such accidents."

Relatives of the missing waited all day, hoping for good news. Some brought photos of loved ones to show rescuers. Volunteers tried to comfort the families. The national government said it would send experts to help with the investigation. A spokesperson said, "People have the right to live in safe buildings." By late night, rescue teams used lights to work in the dark. Heavy equipment lifted large pieces of concrete. Some workers wore masks to protect from dust.

Residents who survived told their experiences. Mr. Mishra, who lived on the third floor, said he felt his bed shaking. He ran outside as the walls started falling. His wife and son were trapped under broken cement, but were pulled out by neighbors. Another woman, Miss Rana, said she called her mother on the phone just before the building fell. She survived with minor injuries. Psychologists visited the shelter to help people with shock and fear.

The incident raised questions about the city’s building safety rules. Many people blamed corruption and lack of inspections. A man whose cousin was missing said, "Authorities take bribes and allow bad construction." The opposition party demanded answers from the government. Some accused the construction firm of using cheap materials. The firm refused to comment. Police said they would question engineers and builders who worked on the collapsed building. The investigation could take weeks.

People from other cities sent messages of support. Social media was filled with posts demanding justice for the victims. Some users shared tips on how to check for unsafe buildings. The disaster was the worst building collapse in the city in ten years. In 2014, another residential building fell, killing eight people. Afterwards, the government announced new safety steps, but many say not much changed.

Engineers from the university visited the site. They took samples of the broken concrete to test in the lab. They said old concrete can lose strength if water enters and rusts the steel bars inside. The weather was dry on Tuesday, so rain was not a reason for the collapse. Some experts said vibrations from nearby construction may have harmed the foundation. Others blamed years of poor repair and ignored warnings from residents.

World scientists have discovered a new change in the reefs of the ocean. The research was released on Thursday in the city of Canberra. The study took place in different seas and focused on reefs. They found something special about sharks near these places. Experts believe the number of shark species is dropping in many parts of the world. Some species are disappearing from the well-known coral reefs. This is because water temperatures are warming. Scientists think climate change is the main reason for this.

The team has been observing the reefs for several years. During this time, many coral structures started to lose color. This is called bleaching. It happens when the water gets too hot for a long time. Without healthy coral, small fish and other creatures cannot stay. Sharks also leave. In some reefs, researchers noticed only one or two types of sharks remained. In the past, those areas had many more species.

This finding is worrying for marine experts. They say if this situation continues, the balance in the ocean could change. Sharks are important for healthy reefs. When there are fewer sharks, other fish numbers grow too fast. This can hurt the reef even more. Some experts call sharks the ‘guardians’ of the reef. If they go away, the coral is in more danger.

Besides temperature, scientists found other problems. Fishing is also affecting shark numbers. Even when fishing is not allowed near reefs, illegal boats come at night. They catch sharks for their fins or meat. Sometimes, sharks get trapped by accident in nets meant for other fish. The team says stronger rules may be needed. They also want people to learn about why sharks are important for the ocean.

The report also describes how weather is becoming less predictable. Storms are more powerful. When strong waves hit a reef, it can break the coral. After the damage, it is hard for new coral to grow. Small animals have trouble surviving. Sharks must travel farther to find food. Young sharks are especially at risk. They need safe places with lots of fish.

The research group used underwater cameras and special sensors. They spent many months gathering information. The team leader, Dr. Sarah Lin, said they saw big changes from year to year. She explained that in 2010, they could see up to ten shark species in one part of the reef. In 2023, only three or four were there. This makes it harder for the reef to recover after disasters like bleaching or storms.

Some local people are also worried. In the Pacific, islanders have seen fewer sharks near their homes. They say the ocean feels empty. Fishers catch less now. Tourism is suffering too. Visitors come to see healthy coral and big fish like sharks. If these disappear, there are fewer jobs for local families.

The authors of the study say solving these problems is not easy. The oceans are connected. Changes in one place can affect others far away. They advise working together, across countries, to protect reefs and sharks. They ask for governments to make new agreements and spend money on ocean science. They also suggest teaching children about the ocean. Dr. Lin is hopeful people will listen. If action comes soon, she believes reefs and sharks can recover.

Experts agree this is a warning for the world. Coral reefs help protect coasts from storms. They give homes to thousands of creatures. They are important for food and jobs. The loss of sharks shows reefs are in trouble. Scientists say everyone must care for the ocean, before it is too late.

Celtic Football Club confirmed on Monday that several players have tested positive after a recent trip to Dubai. The club informed that the players received positive test results following routine checks after their return to Scotland. The club said it is cooperating with the local health authorities. All players who have been affected have entered isolation. The club emphasized that all health protocols were followed during the trip.

Celtic traveled to Dubai last week, which caused some discussion among supporters and the media. Many fans were worried about the risks of traveling during the pandemic. The club said that the trip was planned before the new restrictions and that all staff and players followed strict procedures. The club said the trip was important for the team to prepare for the next matches.

Officials said that the players who did not test positive must train separately and avoid contact with the isolated group. Match plans may change if further positive cases are detected. The club promised to provide updates if the situation develops.

The Scottish football authorities expressed concern about the club’s decision to travel. They asked the club to provide a report about the trip and to explain why travel was necessary. Only players with negative results are allowed to take part in activities. The positive tests affected both first team players and some coaching staff.

Fans reacted with disappointment and frustration on social media. Many supporters said the trip should not have happened. They criticized the club for taking unnecessary risks. Some fans called for club leaders to explain their decisions. Others said the club should apologize if mistakes were made.

The club said there were no plans at this time to cancel upcoming matches. However, it admitted that the situation can change quickly depending on more test results. The club’s next opponent is waiting for further information before confirming the match will go ahead.

A recently published report has caused much discussion in the country. The report, which was revealed on Thursday by the Commission for Inquiry, contains many pages about the homes for children and mothers that were run by various organizations during the last century. According to the report, more than 10,000 children and mothers passed through these homes. Many of them did not leave with good memories. Some did not survive at all. The commission said survivors told of harsh conditions, hunger, and sadness. Many suffered as babies.

Some mothers reported being told nothing about where their children had gone. Some later discovered their child had died. Survivors spoke about feelings of loss that lasted for decades. The commission pointed to many failings by those who ran the homes and those who were supposed to check on them.

Among the findings in the report, the commission said that very young children and babies were often underfed. Many former residents described being always hungry. Meals were small and lacked variety. Some survivors said food was sometimes spoiled, or little was given to babies. The report said that this did not seem to be due to lack of money. Sometimes the homes received enough public funds for better care. The commission said the staff at the homes were often unkind, and sometimes cruel. Punishment was common, both for mothers and children. Some women told the commission they were forced to do hard work while recovering from childbirth. A small number of people told the commission they discovered by accident that they had spent their first years in one of the homes. Their adoptive parents had not been told the real story.

The commission gathered information by interviewing over four hundred former residents of the homes, both mothers and people who had lived there as children. The interviews lasted several months. Many survivors spoke for the first time about their experiences. During the hearings, some women broke down in tears because the memories were too painful. One woman said, “We were never allowed to hold our babies. I remember the sound of them crying.” Another said, “They punished me for asking about my child. They said I should forget her.”

Some survivors said that, as adults, they spent years searching for the graves of siblings or their own children with no answers. The commission described this practice as deeply upsetting and against basic respect for families.

In the city where the excitement for car racing always runs high, there was a new kind of event last weekend. People gathered not only for the speed, but for something else too. Formula One was in town, but now it was not just about the drivers and their machines. There was a different mood because of environmental focus. Usually you would hear engines and see fans waving flags. This time, there were also banners talking about the planet.

Her voice echoed in the stadium, and many looked thoughtful. Later, she posted online about the event and the need for racing to care about environment. Some fans agreed, saying that sport can lead to positive change. A few thought it was strange to mix racing and environmental messages. They said it is not what Formula One is known for.

A spokesperson explained that the old cooling systems were not friendly for the air. The new ones use materials which break down better and use less electricity. Engineers also said that the cars have changed a little to make them less noisy and less wasteful.

Racing teams did not all agree about these changes. One team leader said during an interview that it is cool to try something new. He mentioned they have also started using recycled materials for uniforms and helmets. Another driver said he likes the idea but is worried about the effect on the car’s speed. He told reporters that Formula One is about winning. He wondered if these rules will make races less exciting. His teammate did not mind, he said it is the future and we have to change with it.

Fans noticed that the usual smell of burning rubber was softer this time. Some young visitors said they liked the cleaner smell. They pointed out how the track looked brighter. Vendor stalls also offered different food, with less meat and more plant-based dishes. One family commented that the choices were healthier and even better for the earth. After the races, Goulding attended a talk with engineers and students. She listened as they explained how the new rules work. She nodded and shared stories about her own changes for the planet. Brick homes stood longer, but many lost windows and walls. School classrooms filled with debris. Hospital staff worked almost without rest. They had to treat many people for cuts and broken bones.

International aid groups started to fly supplies in. United Nations teams gave out bottled water, crackers, and tarpaulins. Doctors Without Borders set up tents and treated those with fever or wounds. Volunteers shared more photos for the world to see. One photo’s caption described the silence after the hurricane, broken only by helicopters. Animals wandered the ruined neighborhoods, hungry and afraid. Survivors slept outside, waiting for help or news. In the evenings, families gathered by candles and shared stories of what happened when the wind came.

In some neighborhoods, water levels rose by two meters. People climbed roofs, or took shelter in attics. Later, some rescue stories became famous. One man swam through wind and rain to reach his neighbor, who could not walk. He brought them food wrapped in plastic. Another story told of a nurse in Freeport who used her own car to drive patients to the hospital, even as water reached the door. Social media helped families find each other. Photos of missing people were posted with names and last-known locations. Some were found safe. Others have not returned.

Some residents started to clean up as soon as the wind stopped. They used buckets to carry water out of homes, and swept mud from floors. They hung wet clothes and blankets outside, hoping the sun would return. Volunteers gave out bread and water. In some places, there was no electricity even after a week. Generators became important. People waited in line to charge phones or fill water bottles.

Some people left the islands. They traveled by boat to Nassau or to Florida. Others decided to stay and help rebuild. The government promised money for repairs, but many said it would not be fast. Aid workers warned about sickness from the dirty water. They gave out medicine and taught people how to boil water before drinking it. The government set up shelters in churches and schools. Families crowded together, sometimes three or four in a room. Children painted pictures to show the storm. Some of these were posted next to photos from the hurricane.

The man estimates the value to be near several million dollars. He says the digital currency was stored on his drive. The drive was thrown away by mistake years ago. The man thought he could recover the files. Now, he faces many challenges.

The man worked with computers and technology in the past. At the time, Bitcoin was not widely known. He bought the coins when the price was low. He kept his digital wallet on a drive for safety. He did not expect this wallet would later be so valuable. The wallet is linked to more than eight thousand Bitcoins. The worth has risen over recent years. It has become a big topic for people who follow the cryptocurrency markets. CNN has covered this search in several reports.

The man lives in Newport. He said he realized he lost his hard drive after cleaning his house. He mixed the drive with other trash and took it to a landfill. After discovering the mistake, he started asking officials at the landfill for help. However, the landfill has strict rules. The area is large, and many trucks bring trash daily. The drive is somewhere under thousands of tons of waste. Some officials are not willing to allow a search, saying it may cause health risks.

Over the years, the man has asked for permission. He has submitted plans to recover the drive. He said he would pay for the costs. He said he would share some of the Bitcoin value with the town. He met with city leaders, but his plans were rejected. Many worries exist about safety, pollution, and the costs of searching. There is fear the search might damage local land and cause more problems. The city leaders said the risks do not justify the effort.

The man tried to get attention from more people. He used online forums. He contacted news organizations. CNN and other outlets reported his story. Many Bitcoin fans offered ideas, but few could help with the search. The man offered rewards to those who can find the drive. Some volunteers wanted to join. Still, the city administration has not changed its position.

The man explained that Bitcoin can only be accessed with the correct private key. This key is stored on his missing drive. Without the drive, the coins are locked. No one can spend them or move them. The man said he has searched other places but found nothing. He believes the drive is still at the landfill. He is confident that, if found, the Bitcoins would still be on the drive. Many experts agree it is possible if the drive is not damaged.

As the story continues, people discuss the case in Newport and elsewhere. Some say the process of searching for the drive is not realistic. Others say it is worth trying, because the value is so high. The man said he would keep asking for help. He is not giving up. He hopes rules will change one day, so he can try again.

The case has brought questions about digital currency and safety. Many users are reminded to protect their wallets and keys. The man admitted he did not think about the risk. He said he regrets not making backups. He said he has received messages from people who lost coins in similar ways. There is interest in finding solutions to prevent more losses.

Local authorities in Newport have said there is no change in policy. The landfill is still closed to such searches. Officials say they are not planning to allow digging for lost items. They also say they are not responsible for private losses.

The man is sharing his story to warn others. He says he keeps watching the price of Bitcoin. He describes the experience as difficult. Many people continue to follow updates. Some wonder if the drive will ever be found. For now, the question remains open.

The Olympic organizing committee confirmed on Tuesday that one athlete tested positive for COVID-19. The athlete belonged to the swimming team that arrived at the Olympic Village two days before. The association said the athlete was fully vaccinated and showed no symptoms. The team is staying at a designated hotel near the stadium. Team officials explained that all members have been isolated from others. The athlete is following the instructions of local health authorities.

The committee explained that all athletes, coaches, and staff must take PCR tests every day. Those who test positive should follow the special health guidelines made for the Games. For non-serious cases, the person stays isolated until two negative results are received. For serious cases, hospitalization is needed. The association stated that this protocol is based on advice from international and local doctors.

The rest of the swimming team members had negative results in the latest test. They will continue their daily testing routine. The games medical officer said the risk of further spread is low but not zero. Officials are checking all close contacts of the infected athlete. So far, there is no sign of transmission among the team or to others in the Village.

For the public, the committee emphasized again the importance of health safety. All fans must keep distance and wear masks, even outdoors. Food will only be available in takeaway containers. Spectators are not allowed to gather in groups or stand on seats. The association said these rules are strict to prevent outbreaks. Local citizens are also advised not to organize large private watching events.

This Olympics already had strict border checks and health screenings for all arrivals. Last week, two foreign coaches from another team also had positive results. They were placed in hotel quarantine. Their teams continued competing after new tests were negative.

The Games have not considered postponement after these positive cases. The committee said the schedule remains unchanged at this time. International Olympic officials stated that these measures make the event as safe as possible in the current situation.

The Olympic Village continues to operate with special sanitary rules. Shared spaces are cleaned several times each day. Transport between venues is only allowed with permission and monitoring. The organizers believe the combination of vaccination, testing, and isolation helps keep the Games going. They said they are prepared to react quickly if more infections occur. They are working with health authorities daily to monitor the situation.

Millions of Americans struggle to buy homes. The real estate market shows many differences across groups. For black homebuyers, it can be harder to get a mortgage from banks. Some say credit scores are one problem. Black families often have lower scores because of past events. This affects their chances to become homeowners.

Many first-time buyers want to own property. They look for options in cities and suburbs. Housing prices rise in many places. People wait longer to buy. They save money for a down payment, but sometimes it is not enough. Banks want buyers to have a good credit history. This makes it tough for those who have missed payments years ago.

Studies say black households earn less income than white households. This adds trouble to buying homes. They cannot save as much. Some decide to rent instead. The gap between owners and renters grows larger. Policy experts worry about this situation. They propose programs for lower fees and loans with easier terms. These programs sometimes help, but not everyone qualifies.

Homeownership rates for black Americans stay lower than the national average. In some regions, the numbers are much smaller. Many families face barriers no matter where they live. Lenders can be strict. They check credit scores, past debts, and job history. If buyers cannot show stable work, the loan is denied. Many younger people feel discouraged.

The market changes every year. Some years see fast growth. More people try to buy homes. Other years, prices fall. This affects all buyers, but the impact is more for groups with smaller savings. Black buyers say they need fairer rules. They want banks to consider other factors besides credit scores. Some loan programs do this, but not all banks use them.

Housing agencies notice these problems. They issue reports and statistics. The reports show differences in loan approvals. Black buyers get fewer approvals even when they earn similar wages. The agencies suggest more training for lenders. They also ask for new rules to make loans fair. Changes can be slow.

Many use community organizations for advice.

Black buyers often look for areas with good schools. They want safe neighborhoods. But these places are expensive.

The government offers grants for first-time buyers. Some grants are given to minorities. They help pay for a down payment. But the grants do not cover all costs. Families still need savings. Experts say more grants are needed. They want banks to accept smaller down payments if buyers have steady jobs. This is not always allowed. Local rules can be strict.

Interest rates have gone up this year. Monthly payments are larger. Some buyers pull out of deals. Black buyers are hit hard. Their budgets are smaller than average. They must look for cheaper homes or wait longer. In some cases, they cannot buy at all. Rent prices go up too. Families spend more money on rent and cannot save.

Housing costs are part of a bigger issue. Black homeowners pay more taxes in some areas. Repairs cost extra money. Insurance is needed in many neighborhoods. If a family gets behind, banks may take back the house. This risk scares some buyers away. Experts suggest new programs for repair loans and tax relief.

Police monitored these gatherings but did not make many arrests.
